lit.\u0027\u003c/table\u003e\u003cp class=\":
"

Didactic model: Rf = 1/(1 + e0.7(p − e)), with p the polarity of the compound and e the strength of the eluent.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003ehexa:
"

With hexane (nonpolar) almost nothing moves; with methanol everything rises with the front. Mixtures are tried until the spots lie between Rf 0.2 and 0.8 and are well separated (ΔRf ≥ 0.1–0.15). Change the eluent and watch the elution order: nonpolar first.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn \u003cb\u003ecroma:
"

In adsorption chromatography the stationary phase (silica, polar) retains compounds in proportion to their polarity; the mobile phase (eluent) carries them along. A nonpolar compound travels farther; a polar one stays near the origin. A more polar eluent “competes” with the silica and moves everything faster.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003epl:
"

On the TLC plate the sample is spotted on the baseline and placed in a chamber with eluent. The solvent rises by capillary action. When the plate is removed the front is marked. The retention factor is Rf = dcompound/dfront, always between 0 and 1. An Rf of 0.3–0.5 is usually ideal for separating.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ecolum:
"

The column is TLC at preparative scale: the sample is loaded on top of the silica and eluted. The bands descend at different speeds, and fractions are collected in tubes. The elution volume is Ve = V0(1 + k′), with k′ = (1 − Rf)/Rf. The fractions are followed by TLC.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara que dos compuest:
"

For two compounds to separate, the difference in Rf must be sufficient and the spots narrow (do not overload the plate). On a column, the resolution Rs compares the distance between peaks with their width; Rs ≥ 1.5 indicates complete separation.

"

lit.\u0027Aumenta la polaridad del eluyente: 'Increase the eluent polarity until Rf sits between 0.3 and 0.5.'
lit.\u0027Cada curva es un compuesto; línea: "Each curve is one compound; vertical line = current eluent."
lit.\u0027Dos manchas se separan bien si ΔRf: "Two spots separate well if ΔRf is large and the spots are small"
lit.\u0027Eluye con hexano: los compuestos p: 'Elute with hexane: polar compounds barely move.'
lit.\u0027en la placa, la línea celeste es e: 'on the plate, the light blue line is the solvent front; each spot travels Rf × the distance of the front.'
lit.\u0027En sílice, el compuesto que sale p: "On silica, the compound that comes out first is the most…"
lit.\u0027En una columna, el compuesto más p: "On a column, the most polar compound…"
lit.\u0027La columna aplica el mismo princip: "The column applies the same principle at preparative scale."
lit.\u0027La sílice (polar) retiene más a lo: "Silica (polar) retains polar compounds more; the eluent carries them along"

lit.\u0027Marca los compuestos de la muestra: "Mark the compounds in the sample, choose the eluent and press “Run TLC” or “Column”."
lit.\u0027Más polar → Rf mayor. Ajusta hasta: "More polar → higher Rf. Adjust until the spots separate"
lit.\u0027No logra desplazar los compuestos: "It cannot displace the compounds from the silica."
lit.\u0027Pasa a la columna: el compuesto má: 'Switch to the column: the least polar compound elutes first.'
lit.\u0027Picos gaussianos en V = V₀(1 + k′): "Gaussian peaks at V = V₀(1 + k′) with width proportional to √V."
lit.\u0027Rf = distancia del compuesto / dis: "Rf = distance of the compound / distance of the solvent front"
